title: Revision: Computer Vision and Neural Networks
status: Draft practice quiz; teacher review required
instructions: Ten publicly answerable practice questions from the Course and Laboratory. Results remain only in your browser; not an official exam grade.

questions.prompt: What describes one handwritten image in the Week 8 experiment?
options: 8 numbers from 0 to 255
64 numbers from 0 to 16
One text string containing the digit
Three RGB channel averages
questions.explanation: An 8×8 grid contains 64 block-activity counts, each between 0 and 16.

questions.prompt: What was kept out of training when building the classifier?
options: 200 different labelled images
Only the number zero
All 600 training images
The teacher's handwritten notes
questions.explanation: Two hundred images were withheld so we can evaluate on examples not used in the model's neighbour search.

questions.prompt: Why is predicting handwritten digits supervised learning?
options: It has no examples
It receives known digit labels for its training images
It only groups images without labels
It uses a human-written threshold without learning
questions.explanation: The training images each have a known target digit, and predictions use those labelled examples.

questions.prompt: With k=3, a k-nearest-neighbour classifier does what?
options: Creates three clusters from unlabelled images
Selects three closest labelled training examples to vote
Uses three neural layers
Tests each digit three times then memorises the answer
questions.explanation: k is the number of labelled neighbours voting, not the number of unsupervised clusters.

questions.prompt: For Q=(2,1) and A=(2,4), what is squared Euclidean distance?
The nearest training labels are 8, 1 and 8. What is the 3-NN prediction?
options: The mean 5.67
Undetermined because digits cannot be voted on
questions.explanation: Two votes go to digit 8 and one to digit 1.

questions.prompt: If 196 of 200 held-out predictions are correct, what is accuracy?
questions.explanation: 196/200=0.98, or 98% correct on that specific subset.

questions.prompt: Which observation is a genuine error in the model's default test?
options: A 1 incorrectly predicted as 8
A pixel that has intensity 16
A model using 64 features
A properly withheld image
questions.explanation: Held-out example 17 is truly a 1 but is predicted as an 8 with k=3.

questions.prompt: Select ALL statements supported by an evaluation of 200 held-out images.
options: The result concerns those specific 200 examples
The model will be correct on every camera photo
Its test errors should be examined
A 98% test score guarantees 98% calibrated confidence for each answer
questions.explanation: A finite held-out result supports limited empirical claims. It does not establish universal accuracy or calibrated probabilities.

questions.prompt: Select ALL sensible rules for a fair comparison of a pixel threshold.
options: Keep the test examples fixed
Secretly replace all incorrect predictions with known answers
Compare results before and after the threshold change
Report any changed score without its dataset denominator
questions.explanation: A controlled experiment changes one feature-processing choice while retaining the same examples and reporting the denominator.
